outcomes.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
outcomes.answer: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]

outcomes.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
outcomes.answer:
Making poor capacity decisions can lead to sitting on expensive idle resources or experiencing the performance implications of limited capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Resource saturation when demands exceed capacity is a common cause of failure in on-premises workloads. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]
In the cloud, organizations can monitor demand and utilization to automate adding or removing resources, maintaining optimal levels without over-provisioning or under-provisioning. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]

outcomes.question: What is the difference between one-way door and two-way door decisions?
outcomes.answer:
Two-way door decisions are reversible and can utilize a lightweight process. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
One-way door decisions are hard or impossible to reverse and necessitate more inspection before making them. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
One-way door decisions that could be irreversible should be centralized, whereas two-way door decisions can be made by lower-level organizational leaders. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 26]

outcomes.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
outcomes.answer:
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a cloud service providing a consistent process to review and measure architecture using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The tool offers recommendations to make workloads more reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
AWS provides this service for reviewing workloads at no charge. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
It helps review approaches prior to development, workload states prior to production, and workload states in production. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]
Using the tool, you can compare workloads against the latest AWS architectural best practices, monitor their overall status, and identify potential risks. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What does recovery time objective (RTO) mean?
outcomes.answer:
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the maximum acceptable delay between the interruption of service and restoration of service. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
RTO determines what is considered an acceptable time window when service is unavailable and is defined by the organization. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
Unlike Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR), RTO represents a target or maximum value allowed for a single availability-impacting event. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 19]

outcomes.question: How should a client retry failed requests without overloading a service?
outcomes.answer:
Clients should use exponential backoff to retry requests after progressively longer intervals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Introducing jitter to client retries randomizes intervals and prevents requests from aligning into spikes. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
A maximum number of retries or elapsed time should be configured to prevent backlogs that result in metastable failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Retries should be implemented at only one level of the application stack. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]

outcomes.question: Why should a workload be aware of service quotas and constraints?
outcomes.answer:
Monitoring and automated management of service quotas and resource constraints can proactively reduce failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
Reaching service quotas and constraints can lead to service degradation or disruption within AWS accounts. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
When a constraint is reached unexpectedly, an account's applications or services can become degraded or disrupted. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 24]
Service quotas are established to avoid accidentally provisioning excess resources and to guard services against abuse by limiting API operation request rates. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 469]

outcomes.question: How does the reliability pillar suggest recovering automatically from failures?
outcomes.answer:
Workloads should be monitored for key performance indicators (KPIs) to trigger automation when a threshold is breached. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 12]
The monitored KPIs should measure business value rather than technical operational aspects of the service. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 12]
This monitoring enables automated notification, tracking of failures, and recovery processes that work around or repair the failure. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 12]
More sophisticated automation allows workloads to anticipate and remediate failures before they occur. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: Who is responsible for what in the shared responsibility model for security?
outcomes.answer:
Security and compliance is a shared responsibility between AWS and the customer. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS is responsible for Security of the Cloud, protecting the infrastructure that runs all services offered in the AWS Cloud. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS operates, manages, and controls the components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to physical facility security. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Customer responsibility is Security in the Cloud, which is determined by the AWS Cloud services selected. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
The customer is responsible for managing the guest operating system, associated application software, and security group firewall configurations. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.question: How should secrets and credentials be managed and rotated?
outcomes.answer:
The recommended approach to secrets management is to follow the guidance of remove, replace, and rotate. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 299]
Workloads should replace required long-term credentials with temporary or short-term credentials where possible. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 299]
Credentials such as application and database passwords should be stored in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation established if possible. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 301]
AWS Secrets Manager is purpose-built to securely manage credentials and handle the storage, use, and rotation of API tokens, passwords, and other secrets. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 51]
Organizations should audit and rotate credentials periodically to limit how long credentials can be used to access resources. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 58]
Human exposure to credentials should be reduced by restricting management access to a dedicated IAM role assumed only by a small subset of operational users. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 303]

outcomes.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
outcomes.answer:
The principle of least privilege states that identities should only be permitted to perform the smallest set of actions required to carry out a specific task. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
This principle balances usability, efficiency, and security. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
Operating under the principle of least privilege helps restrict unintended access and track who has access to what resources. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]

outcomes.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
outcomes.answer:
The operational excellence pillar recommends making frequent, small, and reversible changes to workloads. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Workloads should be designed to be scalable and loosely coupled so that components can be updated regularly. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Combining automated deployment techniques with smaller, incremental changes reduces the blast radius and enables faster reversal when failures occur. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Using frequent, small, and reversible changes with change management, configuration management, and build and delivery systems leads to more effective troubleshooting and faster remediation with the ability to roll back changes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 119]

outcomes.question: What are runbooks used for?
outcomes.answer:
A runbook is a documented process containing a series of steps to achieve a specific outcome. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
In cloud operations, runbooks are used to reduce risk and achieve desired outcomes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks serve as codified processes that yield consistent outcomes for tasks ranging from onboarding new team members to deploying major releases. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks are commonly used for routine activities to achieve specific outcomes, unlike playbooks which are used to respond to incidents and non-routine events. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Even in highly automated workloads, runbooks are used for running game days and meeting reporting and auditing requirements. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]

outcomes.question: How can feature flags and A/B testing be used to experiment safely?
outcomes.answer:
Feature flags and A/B testing can be utilized to conduct experiments in a safe manner while collecting user feedback. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]
A/B testing is employed for new features to validate them against real user feedback. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]
AWS AppConfig Feature Flags can be used to create feature flags. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]
A new version of a function can be deployed for beta testing using AWS Lambda versions. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]
Supporting A/B testing or using feature flags may require modifications to application code. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 74]

outcomes.question: What does democratize advanced technologies mean in the performance efficiency pillar?
outcomes.answer:
Democratizing advanced technologies means making advanced technology implementation easier for a team by delegating complex tasks to the cloud vendor. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Rather than having an IT team learn about hosting and running a new technology, teams can consider consuming the technology as a service. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Technologies that require specialized expertise, such as NoSQL databases, media transcoding, and machine learning, become services in the cloud that teams can consume. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
This allows the team to focus on product development rather than managing and provisioning resources. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.question: What is mechanical sympathy?
outcomes.answer:
Mechanical sympathy involves understanding how cloud services are consumed and always using the technology approach that aligns with your workload goals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]
An example of considering mechanical sympathy is taking data access patterns into account when selecting database or storage approaches. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 45]

outcomes.answer:
In-memory databases can be used for application caching, session management, and gaming leaderboards. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 744]
AWS in-memory database services include Amazon ElastiCache and Amazon MemoryDB for Redis. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 744]

outcomes.question: How should failed Lambda transactions be retained and retried?
outcomes.answer:
A dead-letter queue mechanism should be used to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
AWS Lambda allows failed transactions to be sent to a dedicated Amazon SQS dead-letter queue on a per-function basis. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Within AWS Lambda, Maximum Retry Attempts, Maximum Record Age, and Destination on Failure can be configured to control retries while processing data records. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Step Functions should be used whenever possible to minimize custom try/catch, back-off, and retry logic in serverless applications. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
A Step Functions integration can be used to save failed state runs and their state into a DLQ. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]

outcomes.question: What does Amazon API Gateway provide for serverless microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon API Gateway hosts RESTful HTTP requests and responses to customers. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 15]
In a RESTful microservices scenario, Amazon API Gateway provides built-in authorization, throttling, security, fault tolerance, request and response mapping, and performance optimizations. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 15]
The capability to make synchronous calls from Amazon API Gateway to AWS Lambda enables the creation of fully serverless applications. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 12]
API Gateway logging can be utilized to gain visibility into microservices consumer access behaviors. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 15]

outcomes.question: What options does AWS offer for service discovery of microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon ECS offers integrated service discovery by managing a registry of service names using the Route 53 Auto Naming API. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
For Kubernetes-managed services, AWS contributed to the External DNS project to support unified service discovery. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS Cloud Map provides service discovery capabilities and a service registry for resources such as IPs, URLs, and ARNs. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Service discovery can also be implemented using third-party tools such as HashiCorp Consul, etcd, or Netflix Eureka. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS App Mesh can be used to provide reliable discovery and access of services. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 512]

outcomes.question: What does it mean to adopt a consumption model?
outcomes.answer:
Adopting a consumption model means paying only for the computing resources you require and scaling usage up or down according to business requirements rather than elaborate forecasting. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 52]
Under this model, resources such as development and test environments can be stopped when not in use to achieve potential cost savings of 75%. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 52]

outcomes.question: How does the cost optimization pillar suggest reducing cloud waste?
outcomes.answer:
Organizations should identify and recoup spend associated with cloud waste for resources that have been deployed. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Cloud waste happens when incorrectly-sized resources are created or when different usage patterns are observed instead of what was expected. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
To reduce waste and optimize cloud costs, organizations are advised to follow AWS best practices or seek assistance from their account team and partner. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]

outcomes.question: What does AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery do?
outcomes.answer:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates server-hosted applications and databases from any source into AWS using block-level replication of the underlying server. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It allows an AWS Cloud Region to be used as a disaster recovery target for workloads hosted on-premises or across other cloud providers. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
It can also provide disaster recovery for AWS-hosted workloads consisting solely of applications and databases hosted on EC2. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 26]
When a failover event is triggered, the staged resources automatically create a full-capacity deployment in the target Amazon VPC. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 27]
The service coordinates and orchestrates the recovery of compute resources during a failover or drill. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 692]
